In the first step of N2E, the polynomial-time maximum degree approximation algorithm ensures $2 /3$-node-DP to compute the approximation $ ^*$, and guarantees an edge distance bound of \( 2 ^* \) between neighboring graphs after clipping. This bound holds with probability at least $1 - δ/2$. The second step of N2E, graph clipping, does not consume any privacy budget. In the third step, by group privacy (Lemma~ [ref] ), the edge-DP mechanism with $ ' = / 6 ^*$ and $δ' = δ / 4 ^*$ achieves $( /3, δ/2)$-node-DP when the edge distance bound holds. Since this bound fails with probability at most $δ/2$, the mechanism satisfies $( /3, δ)$-node-DP. By sequential composition (Lemma~ [ref] ), combining all three steps yields an overall $( , δ)$-node-DP for the N2E framework.

In the worst case, all edges incident to nodes with degree exceeding $ ^*$ are removed by the distance-preserving clipping mechanism. By Lemma~ [ref] , with probability at least $1-2β/3$, $N_ ^* (G)$ is bounded by $O(log(log( deg (G))/ β)/ )$. Hence, $ G $ is obtained by clipping edges of at most $O(log(log( deg (G))/ β)/ )$ nodes from $G$ under the same probability. The edge-DP mechanism error $ Err _Q^ edge ( G , /6 ^*, δ/4 ^*, β/3)$ holds with probability at least $1 - β/3$. By the union bound, the total error of the N2E output holds with probability at least $1 - β$, completing the proof.
